title: Oak-Braised Chicken with Garlic and Cannellini Gravy
description: Whole garlic cloves soften in an oak-scented braise and blend with white beans into a creamy dairy-free gravy.
equipment: Immersion blender and deep heatproof jug

ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken thighs
ingredients.note: Use plain, unenhanced poultry. Remove visible fat before weighing.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain chicken-and-water broth without a vegetable blend or added seasoning.

ingredients.name: cooked cannellini beans
ingredients.note: Use plain no-salt-added beans, rinsed and drained.

steps.title: Heat the pellet smoker
steps.text: Load the Traeger Silverton 610 with oak wood pellets. Preheat with the lid closed to 300°F, allowing about 15 minutes.

steps.title: Start the garlic
steps.text: Bring {garlic}, {thyme} and {broth} to a simmer in the Dutch oven on the stovetop. Simmer gently for 6 minutes.

steps.title: Smoke the bean broth
steps.text: Stir {beans} into the broth and set the uncovered Dutch oven on the grate. Close the smoker lid for 12 minutes so the broth picks up the oak smoke.

steps.title: Braise under the lid
steps.text: Nestle {chicken} flat in the hot bean broth. Cover the Dutch oven now as the wrap point. Braise at 300°F for 25–45 minutes until each thigh reaches 175°F in its thickest part.

steps.title: Rest in the braising liquid
steps.text: Transfer the chicken and a ladle of its liquid to a warm bowl. Cover and rest for 5 minutes while finishing the sauce.

steps.title: Puree the gravy base
steps.text: Blend the garlic, beans and braising liquid in the deep jug. Press through a sieve into the HexClad to remove bean skins.

steps.title: Bind the sauce
steps.text: Bring the sauce to a simmer. Whisk in the freshly stirred slurry and let it bubble gently for 1 minute, stirring until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Finish with chives
steps.text: Stir {chives} through the gravy off heat.

steps.title: Sauce and serve
steps.text: Cut the rested thighs into short, thin slices and divide between bowls. Add their resting juices and ladle the white bean gravy over each portion.

notes: Sauce yield: About 1 1/2 cups for two. Make ahead: Cook the beans ahead or refrigerate rinsed no-salt-added canned beans for the next day. Refrigerate shallow portions within 2 hours, or within 1 hour outdoors above 90°F. Use refrigerated leftovers within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. The bean puree protects the meat and comes back together when whisked after thawing. Freeze in individual portions for up to 2 months. Fridge reheat: Warm the chicken in its bean gravy covered in the HexClad over medium-low with a splash of water. Stir or turn occasionally and check from 6 minutes, until the center reaches 165°F. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then follow the fridge reheating directions. For a milder garlic flavor, use half the cloves. The white beans provide the creamy texture without dairy. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 243 kcal, 33.0 g protein, 12.7 g total carbohydrate, 5.9 g fat, 2.3 g fiber, 162 mg sodium. Includes all the chicken and sauce in the listed recipe. Sodium varies with the broth. Fiber is estimated before straining.
